profile.headline: Software Engineer at Boeing | MS Computer Science at Georgia Tech
profile.summary:
I'm currently a Software Engineer at Boeing working in an advanced vehicle autonomy group focused on modern software development targeting maritime platforms. I have deep interests in software, guidance & control and autonomy - especially at the intersection of those three interest areas. I'm always eager to learn and grow outside of my comfort zone  and knowledge areas as I progress through my career.

I am also a graduate of Boeing's Engineering Career Foundation Program (ECFP). ECFP is a competitive, two year rotation program dedicated to developing early career engineering talent at Boeing. Each participant completes four, six-month rotations aimed at building technical breadth by rotating across Boeing's various business units and through the four product lifecycle stages. Through this diverse range of rotations, participants build strong corporate citizenship and a technical skillset beyond that of a typical early career engineer. Additionally, this unique experience provides numerous professional development and networking opportunities across the enterprise. 

Prior to starting ECFP, I spent two years in an advanced Flight Controls group as a Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC) Engineer further developing the skills and knowledge base I acquired during my graduate studies at Washington University in St. Louis.

Always happy to connect and answer any questions!

positions.title: Maritime Autonomous Vehicle Software Engineer III
positions.description:
• Develop Unmanned Maritime Autonomy Architecture (UMAA) compliant C++ vehicle control focused microservices deployable in a Docker containerized Linux environment.
• Modernize Windows based vehicle simulation by establishing automated testing in Jenkins pipeline and supporting environment transition to Linux containers to provide significant time improvement options for legacy program.
• Investigate, propose and receive recognition for exploration of modern software service integration into existing legacy platform.

positions.title: ECFP United States Recruitment Lead
positions.description:
• Coached a 10-person team through detailed review and interviews of multiple high-potential early career candidates across the US.
• Emphasized excellence in communication through transparency and punctuality in updates between management, team members, applicants, HR and other stakeholders.
• Demonstrated strong adaptability and tolerance to schedule risk to maintain on-time review of candidates when faced with several external, unplanned roadblocks.

positions.title: Engineering Career Foundation Program (ECFP)
positions.description:
ECFP is a fast paced, highly selective, prestigious, two-year (comprised of four 6-month rotations) technical and leadership development program for early career engineers to experience multiple engineering functions across the global Boeing enterprise while gaining a wide breadth of industry knowledge and deepening technical skills.

During my time in ECFP, I primarily focused on expanding my technical skillset into the realm of software engineering and development. Most of my rotations enabled me to further learn outside of my comfort zone and continue to gain insightful technical experiences that ultimately enabled me to continue pursuit of software engineering roles upon graduation from the program.

The experiences listed below this section highlight my rotations and leadership experiences during ECFP.

positions.title: ECFP Rotation 4: Autonomous Vehicle Software & GNC Engineer II @ Aurora Flight Sciences
positions.description:
• Modified and scripted previously manual HIL test procedures to fit within growing automated C++ test framework to reduce overhead and provide streamlined regression testing capabilities for software updates targeting an optionally piloted vehicle framework.
• Leveraged MATLAB scripting and GNC data analysis to quickly determine root cause factors to address in future software deliverables.
• Diversified Boeing engineering experience by expanding autonomous vehicle software rapid development knowledge through time spent supporting key subsidiary.

positions.title: ECFP Rotation 3: Maritime Autonomous Vehicle Software Engineer II
positions.description:
• Modeled multiple low and mid-level UMAA microservices using MBSE in Cameo to aid in software solution implementation.
• Developed MATLAB algorithms to interpret backup INU signal messaging for future ADA code integration on legacy platform.
• Successfully demonstrated ability to rapidly learn new technical skills, strong independence and robust team working skills through technical contributions across multiple programs.

positions.title: ECFP Rotation 2: 787 Fleet Chief Office SRP Project Engineer II
positions.description:
• Prepared and presented key action results to major global 787 fleet operators demonstrating successful closure of critical design updates.
• Led technical project management efforts to ensure proper, on time completion of economic and safety Service Related Problems (SRPs) for the 787 fleet.
• Bridged the gap between engineering and operators through strong communication skills and an advanced ability to distill very technical knowledge into the necessary, important components.
• Grew my engineering skillset by expanding current knowledge base through first time project management experience and by taking on SRPs outside previous technical experience areas.

positions.title: ECFP Rotation 1: Training Systems Vehicle Simulation Software Engineer II
positions.description:
• Expanded C++ code base in a SAFe Agile development environment to implement necessary updates to improve training experience.
• Developed modifications to critical training modules and successfully tested, integrated and delivered valuable new capabilities to the multiple immersive training simulators.

positions.title: Phantom Works - Guidance, Navigation & Control (GNC) Engineer II
positions.description:
• Developed GNC algorithms to support fixed-wing autonomy development through advanced control laws design such as OBLTR.
• Managed software development process and testing coordination for internal research program development.
• Synthesized best GNC practices across multiple enterprise business units that traditionally operated independently.

positions.title: Academic 'Plus' Tutor
positions.description:
• Tutored high school students in standardized test preparation and STEM courses through the Advanced Placement level.
• Demonstrated patience and creativity when working with students who struggle to initially grasp core concepts.
• Exceeded expectations by maintaining high satisfaction and retention rates with each client.
• Exceled in and receive recognition for ability to be flexible when serving students and their families.
• Quickly promoted from ‘Regular’ level to ‘Plus’ level tutor in December 2017.

positions.title: Quantitative Physiology Laboratory Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• Instructed students in laboratory setting to be successful with physiological experiments.
• Provided constructive comments to students on graded work.
• Coached students through difficult report problems to enrich their understanding of course material.

company.name: Washington University in St. Louis, Department of Biomedical Engineering

positions.title: Lead Engineering Teaching and Program Assistant
positions.description:
• Managed a small team of teaching assistants by strategizing best methods for ensuring student success of engineering principles.
• Produced 34 written student evaluations and revised over 70 evaluations written by other team members.
• Mastered the ability to simply and clearly explain difficult engineering concepts to students without a formal background.

positions.title: Pre-Medicine Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
• Evaluated student performance through written performance assessments, effectively communicating strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations for improvement. 
• Prepared and taught lessons on pre-medical topics aimed at interested high school students.

honors.title: L. Stephen Boehm Memorial Scholarship
honors.issuer: Issued by Washington University in St. Louis School of Engineering & Applied Science · Sep 2015
